title: All one in Christ (Galatians 3:23–29)
hookLine: neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male and female
tomorrow: is everyone a child of God, or do you have to be adopted?

cards: Every form has the boxes. Check one. Paul writes a sentence that knocks over three of them: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female."
Neither, nor. Neither, nor. Neither, nor.
That's the King James, an even drumbeat. But in Paul's Greek the drumbeat slips. The first two pairs are neither, nor.
The third isn't neither male nor female. It's male and female. Why would a careful writer change the rhythm right at the end?

teach.h: MALE AND FEMALE CREATED HE THEM.
teach.b: Those three words come from the first page of the Bible. Genesis says of human beings: "male and female created he them." Some readers hear Paul pointing straight back there.
What God made in the beginning, God is now gathering into one family. That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: tucked inside a well-known verse about unity is a quiet quotation from creation.
Now look at how Paul gets to the line.
"For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ."
Put on, like clothes. Everyone who comes up out of the water wears the same garment. Then the end of the sentence: "for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

Notice what that doesn't say. Paul goes on writing to Jews and Greeks, to slaves and free people, to women and men. The differences are still there; Galatians never asks anyone to stop being who they are.
What's gone is the ranking. None of these lines decides who belongs at the table.
And then the surprise for yesterday's outsiders: "if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise."
The Gentiles Peter wouldn't eat with turn out to be family, heirs to a promise made to Abraham.

how: Some churches read Galatians 3:27 at baptisms, and in some the newly baptized are given a white garment, a picture of having put on Christ.

s: Galatians 3:28 is about everyone on earth, believers or not
Paul says all one in Christ Jesus, writing to the baptized. tomorrow asks about everyone.
the King James says neither male nor female
it does. the Greek's third pair reads male and female, the words of Genesis.

games.q: your little cousin, reading the King James, hears your uncle say Paul's Greek has 'male AND female.' she asks why. what do you tell her?
o: Paul is echoing Genesis: male and female created he them.
it's a mistake in the Greek that the King James fixed later.
Paul meant men and women must always sit side by side.
games.why: the third pair borrows the words of creation. some readers hear Paul saying what God made in the beginning is being gathered into one family.

practice: Find a pen and a scrap of paper. Write the name of one person on the other side of a divide in your life, a family feud, a team, a faith, and under it one true thing you honor in them. Keep the paper where you'll see it this week.

wordCard.voice: All one in Christ. Paul's line for people who stay different, and stop ranking each other, in one family.

orig.note: Greek: one; 'ye are all one in Christ Jesus', Galatians 3:28.

carryVoice: Keep this line: all one, which was never the same as all alike. Peace to you.
